title: Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris) Cut Stump — Ukrainian / Russian forest-steppe biome

sources.pinus_wiki: Pinus sylvestris — Wikipedia (trunk DBH range; bark description; two-tone bark)
sources.conifers_org: conifers.org — Pinus sylvestris species profile (lower bark thickness, colour and texture)
sources.eu_jrc: EU JRC Forest Atlas — Pinus sylvestris stand dimension tables
sources.research_trees: docs/2026-06-10-nature-research-trees.md — regionally sourced tree dimensions (Scots pine 0.5–1.3 m DBH, upper bark orange-red/copper, lower bark up to 5 cm thick)

trunk_dbh_mm.unit: mm (diameter at breast height, 1.3 m above ground)
trunk_dbh_mm.src: pinus_wiki, eu_jrc — range 500–1300 mm (exceptionally >1700 mm); lower end used for a typical younger forest specimen
trunk_dbh_mm.note: Using 500 mm DBH as a realistic medium-sized pine, not an old-growth giant

trunk_r_mm.unit: mm (cross-section radius at the cut face)

stump_h_mm.unit: mm (height of stump above ground to cut face)
stump_h_mm.src: DESIGN — not quantified in any source; typical chainsaw felling leaves a 300–500 mm stump; 350 mm chosen as a mid-range design value
stump_h_mm.note: Flagged in needs[] — a sourced stump-height standard would supersede this estimate

bark_th_lower_mm.src: conifers_org — Scots pine lower trunk: thick scaly grey-brown deeply fissured plates up to ~5 cm thick

root_flare_r_mm.unit: mm (stump radius at soil level, including root-flare buttresses)
root_flare_r_mm.src: DESIGN — no quantified source found; set at trunk_r_mm × 1.24 (24% wider at base, a typical visual proportion for pine root flares)

root_flare_h_mm.unit: mm (visible height of root-flare zone above soil level)
root_flare_h_mm.src: DESIGN — not directly sourced; set as ~28% of stump height for a visually readable proportion

cut_face_th_mm.unit: mm (stand-proud thickness of the exposed wood disk on top of the stump)
cut_face_th_mm.src: DESIGN — geometric detail; 8 mm reads as a distinct face without excessive bulk

soil_disc_r_mm.unit: mm (radius of the disturbed-soil / moss base disc around the stump)
soil_disc_r_mm.derivation: root_flare_r_mm + 50 mm = 310 + 50 = 360 mm — a thin soil-disturbance disc surrounding the root flare

soil_disc_h_mm.unit: mm (height of the ground-level soil/moss base pad)
soil_disc_h_mm.src: DESIGN — a minimal visual base pad to prevent the stump from looking cut-off at ground level

growth_ring_step_mm.unit: mm (stand-proud height per concentric ring disk on the cut face)
growth_ring_step_mm.src: DESIGN — each ring disk stands 8 mm proud of the one below; matches cut_face_th_mm for visual consistency

construction.bark_lower: Thick scaly grey-brown deeply fissured plates, up to 5 cm thick on lower trunk
construction.bark_upper: Thin flaking orange-red / copper coloured bark on upper trunk and branches
construction.wood_tone: Fresh-cut sapwood: pale yellow to light tan (woodMid); heartwood: slightly darker reddish-brown (woodDark)
construction.growth_rings: Concentric annual rings visible on cut face — alternating lighter earlywood / darker latewood bands
construction.root_flare: Roots flare out at soil level forming low buttresses; darker coloration from soil contact

feature_inventory.src: DESIGN — visual grounding at soil level
conifers_org — darker bark at soil contact
construction — dense dark heartwood at centre

game_model_purpose: World scatter prop — cut pine stump for pine bor, forest-steppe shelterbelts, and shelled front-line forest biomes in ENGENDROS PURGE
needs: Sourced stump height (mm) for a felled Scots pine — no quantified standard found in research; 350 mm (dossier#stump_h_mm) is a design estimate
Sourced root flare radius at soil level (mm) for Pinus sylvestris — no quantified ratio found; 310 mm / 124% of trunk radius (dossier#root_flare_r_mm) is a design estimate
Sourced visible root-flare height above soil (mm) for Pinus sylvestris — 100 mm (dossier#root_flare_h_mm) is a design estimate
